episode.title: Adapt replayed reasoning messages to a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint
episode.before: At parent d50dc84e363f4225193418fcd8844fa21f3ae66a, provider selection had no endpoint-specific adapter for api.fireworks.ai. Requests therefore used the default OpenAI-compatible provider, which, for model names containing qwen3, copied each non-empty assistant reasoning_content value into an additional reasoning field. The pipeline sent that provider-built request outbound, so a multi-turn continuation replaying a thinking response carried both fields to an endpoint that rejects messages[N].reasoning with HTTP 400.
episode.after: At 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a, exact api.fireworks.ai hosts and their subdomains select a dedicated provider. It first retains the default request construction, then creates an outbound message array that removes reasoning only from assistant messages where reasoning is a string exactly equal to reasoning_content. It preserves reasoning_content, distinct caller-supplied reasoning values, source history, and the existing default behavior for other endpoints.
episode.diff: The change adds and exports an endpoint-specific provider, inserts hostname-based selection before the default-provider fallback, and overrides outbound request construction to undo only the default provider's recognizable reasoning mirror. It also adds focused routing and transformation tests plus an HTTP integration test that exercises two-turn history conversion through the real generator/provider path against a strict local endpoint.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a resolves issue #11657 through PR #11701 and identifies the failure as an HTTP 400 caused by a mirrored reasoning field on replayed Qwen3 thinking turns.

In the parent state, DefaultOpenAICompatibleProvider.buildRequest detects qwen3 in the request model and maps assistant messages through mirrorReasoningContentToReasoning, which copies a non-empty reasoning_content value into reasoning when reasoning is not already a string.
ContentGenerationPipeline delegates the converted request to this.config.provider.buildRequest before the request proceeds through later wire-shape processing.
evidence_units.source: git show 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a:packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/pipeline.ts, around providerRequest construction at line 951

evidence_units.claim: The change inserts Fireworks provider selection after existing known-provider checks and before the default-provider fallback.
Endpoint detection parses baseUrl and matches only the lowercase hostname api.fireworks.ai or a hostname ending in .api.fireworks.ai; absent or invalid URLs do not match.
The dedicated provider calls the default provider first and then maps the resulting messages through unmirrorReasoningField, placing compatibility adaptation at the outbound provider boundary.

The adapter changes only assistant messages whose reasoning is a string equal to reasoning_content; it returns other messages unchanged and removes the matching reasoning property by constructing a new object.

Unit tests verify removal of the mirrored field for the canonical host and subdomains, preservation of reasoning_content and source history, rejection of a hostile suffix hostname, preservation of a distinct explicit reasoning value, and unchanged mirroring on non-matching endpoints.
evidence_units.source: git show 3ba01990e13e9e8e14e147b60add50e0f972431a:packages/core/src/core/openaiContentGenerator/provider/fireworks.test.ts, describe('Fireworks provider reasoning-mirror suppression')

evidence_units.claim: An HTTP integration test drives two generateContent turns through OpenAIContentGenerator and a strict local endpoint; the endpoint would return the reproduced 400 when an assistant message contains reasoning, while the asserted follow-up wire message retains reasoning_content, omits reasoning, and receives a successful response.

evidence_units.claim: The commit adds 407 lines across provider registration, implementation, and tests, with no modification to the shared default-provider mirroring implementation.

The supplied GitHub bundle lacks the issue body, comments, timeline, PR body, reviews, and status checks; its usable GitHub evidence is limited to issue/PR identity, commit linkage, changed files, and provenance metadata.

candidate_atomics.name: route_endpoint_by_canonical_hostname
candidate_atomics.title: Select the compatibility adapter from the canonical endpoint hostname
candidate_atomics.description: Recognize an endpoint using parsed hostname boundaries and route matching requests to its dedicated compatibility adapter without relying on model-family names or substring matches.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure requests reach the adapter that implements the actual endpoint contract while avoiding false routing for similarly named or hostile hosts.
semantic_action.pre_state: A configured OpenAI-compatible base URL would otherwise fall through to the generic provider, and the served model name is not sufficient evidence of the endpoint implementation.
semantic_action.post_state: The canonical endpoint hostname and its subdomains select the dedicated adapter; unrelated, malformed, and suffix-confusable hosts do not.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise canonical-host, subdomain, hostile-suffix, and unrelated-host cases and assert the resulting request behavior identifies the selected provider path.

candidate_atomics.name: remove_only_derived_incompatible_field
candidate_atomics.title: Remove only the derived field rejected by the endpoint
candidate_atomics.description: At the outbound boundary, recognize the exact compatibility field synthesized by shared request construction and remove that copy without altering source history or legitimate fields.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent strict endpoints from rejecting replayed structured messages while retaining the information they accept and preserving caller-authored values.
semantic_action.pre_state: Shared request construction has produced assistant messages where a derived field may equal its source field, but the selected endpoint rejects the derived field during multi-turn replay.
semantic_action.post_state: Outbound assistant messages omit the derived field only when it is the recognizable string copy of the source field; the source field, distinct explicit values, non-assistant messages, and original history remain intact.
semantic_action.validation: Assert field-level behavior for equal and distinct values and run a multi-turn generator request against a strict endpoint that rejects the incompatible field, inspecting the accepted wire body.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt_shared_request_shape_for_strict_endpoint
candidate_workflows.title: Adapt a shared request shape for a stricter compatible endpoint
candidate_workflows.description: Route only the affected endpoint to a narrow outbound adapter, then remove the provably derived incompatible field while preserving shared behavior and caller data.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow multi-turn replay through a strict OpenAI-compatible endpoint without sending a shared-layer compatibility field that the endpoint rejects.
when_to_use: A nominally compatible endpoint rejects a field synthesized by shared request construction rather than supplied independently by the caller.
The failure occurs after prior structured assistant output is replayed, including continuations following thinking or tool-use turns.
The endpoint can be identified from configuration using a canonical hostname boundary.
anti_goals: Do not remove the accepted source field needed to replay prior reasoning.
Do not disable or change shared mirroring behavior for endpoints that accept or require it.
Do not infer endpoint identity from a hosted model-family name.
Do not mutate persisted or caller-owned conversation history.
Do not discard a distinct explicit field merely because it has the same semantic category as the rejected derived field.
not_applicable_when: The endpoint itself requires the derived field or rejects the source field instead.
The rejected value cannot be distinguished from a caller-authored value using an evidence-backed invariant.
Provider identity cannot be established safely from available configuration.
The failure is unrelated to outbound request shape or multi-turn replay.
inputs: Canonical hostname contract for the affected endpoint
Endpoint rejection payload or equivalent reproduced failure
Representative multi-turn history containing the structured assistant field
workflow_graph.entry_state: A shared provider emits both a source field and its synthesized mirror during replay, and requests to one strict endpoint fail before continuation completes.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Only requests routed to the affected endpoint omit the exact synthesized field at the outbound boundary; accepted fields and explicit distinct values survive, other endpoints retain prior behavior, and multi-turn continuation succeeds.

steps.condition: The endpoint has a stable canonical hostname and model names may be served by multiple providers.
steps.validation: Canonical and subdomain URLs select the adapter, while suffix-confusable and unrelated hosts follow their existing provider path.

steps.condition: The selected endpoint rejects the derived field and the shared transformation makes the derived copy recognizable by exact equality with its source.
steps.validation: Unit assertions prove selective removal and preservation; an HTTP integration test proves a replayed multi-turn request reaches the wire without the rejected field and receives a successful response.

validation_ladder: Confirm the parent shared provider actually synthesizes the rejected field for the affected request class.
Test provider routing for the exact hostname, supported subdomains, malformed or unrelated URLs, and hostname-confusion cases.
Test transformation invariants: preserve the accepted source field, preserve distinct explicit values, remove only an equal string mirror, and leave source history unchanged.
Exercise the real conversion, provider, and HTTP path with replayed multi-turn history against a strict endpoint stand-in that reproduces the rejection contract.
Run the focused provider test suite in a materialized checkout with the repository's required Node runtime.
stop_conditions: Stop if the endpoint rejection cannot be reproduced or tied to the synthesized field.
Stop if safe provider identity requires a model-name heuristic shared by unrelated endpoints.
Stop if the implementation cannot distinguish the derived copy from caller-authored data.
Stop if removing the field breaks required replay information or changes unaffected endpoints.
